title: Maximum speed calculation
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be v_max = 0.8 m/s.

title: Constant velocity power
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be P = 4000 W.

title: Acceleration time
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be t = 1/3 s or approximately 0.333 s.

title: Apply power-force-velocity relation
description: Important: For parts (1) and (2), the student must correctly use the formula P = Fv, relating power, force, and velocity.

title: Apply Newton's second law
description: Important: For part (3), the student must set up F_net = ma to find the required traction force F = m(g + a).

title: Identify limiting condition
description: Important: For part (3), the student must recognize that acceleration stops when the required power (Fv) equals the crane's maximum power, solving for the final velocity v.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The solution should maintain consistent SI units (W, m/s, kg, N) throughout the calculations.

title: Sign or force direction error
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly using the net force (e.g., F = mg - ma for upward acceleration) or misapplying the power formula (e.g., P = mgv in all cases).

title: Power vs. force confusion
description: Pitfall: Assuming the crane delivers constant maximum force instead of constant maximum power during the acceleration in part (3).
